Hi Jared — copying a short technical note so the pilot planning is concrete. High level:

1) KMS/HSM:
- Hosted: we offer tenant-level encryption and can support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) in specific regions via a managed integration with major cloud KMS providers. For FIPS/HSM-backed key material our Private option is the path that provides HSM attestation; Hosted with customer-managed keys will meet most enterprise needs but we should validate with your compliance team.

2) Retention and logs:
- Hosted: retention windows are configurable per-route and can be set to 0 (no persistent logs) for sensitive flows. Audit logs are available via our console and can be forwarded to your SIEM.

3) Rate limiting & endpoint buckets (proposal):
- We recommend creating three logical endpoints for the pilot: /ingest (batch calls), /chat (streaming assistant), /embeddings (vector).
- Pilot ratebands (sandbox -> prod expected increases):
  * ingest: sandbox 50 qps -> pilot 200 qps -> production 300+ qps with burst capacity
  * chat: sandbox 10 qps -> pilot 60 qps -> production 150 qps
  * embeddings: sandbox 30 qps -> pilot 200 qps (indexing off-hours) -> production 500 qps (sharded)
- Default Hosted per-endpoint throttle: 100 rps (can be raised for pilot slices after our quick sizing).
- Concurrency: streaming connections are multiplexed; for planning assume concurrency at ~10% of QPS for chat.

4) Performance fallbacks:
- If during pilot we observe tail-latency/regression, we can (a) increase pilot capacity (temporary burst), (b) route heavy traffic to Dedicated if you purchase reserved capacity, or (c) apply model quantization/shorter context windows to maintain SLO.
